symptomShortText: Grinding burn on guide rail raceway ground with WHEEL1 - coolant nozzle misaligned

defect.defectText: Grinding burn and micro-cracks on precision linear guideway

causesIshikawa.description: Grinder operator ran program GR-200-RW as released
WHEEL1 coolant nozzle knocked out of position during wheel change - only 9 l/min reaches the contact zone vs min 25
Dressing every 18 parts as restored after 8D-10049110
Rail blank lot RB-5530 hardness 60 HRC, within specification
Barkhausen probe BN-01 verified on reference sample

fiveWhyChain.question: Why did the raceway show grinding burn?
fiveWhyChain.answer: Barkhausen noise peak reached 74 mp against max 35 mp on rails ground with WHEEL1

fiveWhyChain.question: Why did WHEEL1 overheat the surface?
fiveWhyChain.answer: Coolant at the contact zone was 9 l/min instead of at least 25 l/min

fiveWhyChain.question: Why was coolant missing at the contact zone? (root cause)
fiveWhyChain.answer: The nozzle was knocked out of position during the wheel change and the setup has no nozzle position check

actions.actionText: Perform 100% Barkhausen noise inspection on all rails from batch B-50700
Re-align the coolant nozzle on WC-GRIND-01 wheel 1 and restore coolant flow at the contact zone
Add coolant nozzle position check to the grinder setup checklist on all grinding cells

fmeaLink.description: Thermal grinding burn from insufficient coolant at the contact zone

lessonsLearned.whatWorked: 100% Barkhausen screening stopped every burned rail before assembly
lessonsLearned.whatDidnt: Wheel change setup had no check that the coolant still hits the contact zone

isIsNot.isWhereWhenItHappens: GR-200 raceway - WC-GRIND-01-WHEEL1 - after wheel change on 2026-07-29
isIsNot.isNotWhereWhenItDoesnt: WC-GRIND-01-WHEEL2 - same blank lot RB-5530 and same dressing interval
isIsNot.notes: Defect starts at the wheel change and stays on WHEEL1
